newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Yadav ordered held in judicial custody.
newsitem.headline: India's Yadav ordered held in judicial custody.

text.p: A court in this eastern Indian city on Wednesday ordered Laloo Prasad Yadav, a powerful politician and former chief minister of Bihar state, to be detained in judicial custody, court officials said.

Yadav was ordered to be held in judicial custody until August 6. Under Indian law an accused person can be held in judicial custody for a maximum of two weeks while he is being investigated, and custody can be renewed only if prosecutors present sufficient evidence.
Yadav earlier surrendered before a judge in a special courtroom set up by the federal Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), in front of thousands of cheering supporters.

The Supreme Court paved the way for his arrest on Tuesday by rejecting his appeal against a Bihar court's refusal to grant him "anticipatory bail", allowed under Indian law to people who apprehend arrest. Patna is the state capital.

Yadav was forced to resign last Friday as chief minister of the poor, populous state after weeks of stubborn resistance following his indictment in April by the CBI in a $280 million state farm funds scandal.
